title: East Asia: Chiang Mai → Mekong → Vientiane

days.day: Tuesday, 1st December 2026 - Chiang Mai: Old City

checkpoints.title: Check in inside the Old City
checkpoints.description: Stay inside the moat: temples, cafés and night markets are walkable, Grab for the rest. Flying in? Fill in the free TDAC arrival card within 72 h before landing.

checkpoints.title: Khao soi lunch
checkpoints.description: Chiang Mai's signature coconut-curry noodle soup with crispy noodles on top. Khao Soi Khun Yai by the north moat is a local favourite (lunch only).

checkpoints.title: Warorot Market
checkpoints.description: The locals' market by the river: northern sausages, dried fruit, flower stalls and cheap fabric. Try nam prik noom and pork crackling.

checkpoints.title: Old City temples
checkpoints.description: Wat Phra Singh, then Wat Chedi Luang and its huge half-ruined chedi (stop at the Monk Chat tables and ask the monks anything), and Wat Chiang Man, the oldest temple in town.

checkpoints.title: Thai cooking class
checkpoints.description: Market tour, pound your own curry paste, cook 4–5 dishes, eat all of it. Book a day ahead, e.g. the evening class at Asia Scenic in the Old City.

checkpoints.title: Wat Umong
checkpoints.description: Quiet 700-year-old forest temple at the foot of Doi Suthep, with meditation tunnels under the chedi and 'talking trees' hung with Buddhist proverbs.

checkpoints.title: Thai massage
checkpoints.description: Lila Thai Massage employs women just released from prison and gives them a fresh start. Good cause, great massage.

checkpoints.title: Dinner at Chang Phueak Gate
checkpoints.description: Evening street food at the north gate. The star is the 'Cowboy Hat Lady' with her stewed pork leg on rice (khao kha moo). Live jazz next door at North Gate Jazz Co-Op afterwards.

days.day: Wednesday, 2nd December 2026 - Elephants & Doi Suthep by scooter

checkpoints.title: Elephant Nature Park
checkpoints.description: Rescue sanctuary ~1.5 h north. No riding, no shows: you feed the elephants, walk with the herds and watch them bathe in the river. Book the half-day morning visit online, it sells out.

checkpoints.title: Rent scooters
checkpoints.description: Back in town, rent 125cc scooters for the ride up the mountain (passport or cash deposit). Carry an International Driving Permit (1968 convention) and your licence: police checkpoints are common, and without them travel insurance may not cover you. Helmets are the law.

checkpoints.title: Wat Pha Lat
checkpoints.description: Mossy jungle temple by a waterfall, overlooking the city. ~5 km above the zoo, turn off at the roadside buildings and ride 330 m down. (Walking up the Monk's Trail instead now costs ~€2.50.)

checkpoints.title: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
checkpoints.description: Ride on up to northern Thailand's most sacred temple: the 306-step naga staircase (or the lift) to the golden chedi, the whole city below.

checkpoints.title: Sunset viewpoint
checkpoints.description: 4.5 km further up the road, 500 m below Bhubing Palace. Sunset ~17:45, then ride down slowly: steep road, in the dark.

checkpoints.title: Nimman
checkpoints.description: The hip part of town: cafés, small design shops and One Nimman. Coffee-and-cake o'clock.

checkpoints.title: Northern Thai dinner at Tong Tem Toh
checkpoints.description: Classics in Nimman soi 13: sai oua sausage, nam prik ong dip, gaeng hang lay pork curry. Usually a queue, it moves fast.

days.day: Thursday, 3rd December 2026 - Doi Inthanon, Thailand's highest peak

checkpoints.title: Drive to Doi Inthanon
checkpoints.description: Private car with driver for the day (1–4 people, ~2.5 h each way), booked a day ahead: shared tours leave at 07:00–08:00 and miss the sunrise, and on scooters it is 100 km each way and freezing before dawn. Want to camp instead? Park tents at the HQ campground (km 31) ~€6, book on nps.dnp.go.th: it adds a night but skips the 04:00 start.

checkpoints.title: Sunrise on the Kew Mae Pan trail
checkpoints.description: A 3.2 km loop along a ridge, through cloud forest and open grassland: the classic sunrise spot (~06:45), often above a sea of mist. A local guide is required, hired at the trailhead (~€5.50 per group); opens 06:00.

checkpoints.title: Summit, 2,565 m
checkpoints.description: The highest point in Thailand: a boardwalk loop through the mossy Ang Ka cloud forest and the summit marker.

checkpoints.title: Twin royal pagodas
checkpoints.description: Two chedis built for the King's and Queen's 60th birthdays, with flower gardens and views over the ridges.

checkpoints.title: Lunch at Mae Klang Luang
checkpoints.description: Karen village on the way down, with rice terraces and coffee grown on the mountain.

checkpoints.title: Wachirathan waterfall
checkpoints.description: Big, loud waterfall right by the road down; the spray reaches the viewing platform. Included in the park ticket. Back in Chiang Mai by ~15:30.

checkpoints.title: Night Bazaar & repack
checkpoints.description: Souvenir stroll along Chang Klan Road, then repack: the big bags go to Pai by van tomorrow, keep a daypack for the night in Chiang Dao.

days.day: Friday, 4th December 2026 - Scooters to Chiang Dao

checkpoints.title: One-way scooters to Pai
checkpoints.description: Aya Service rents scooters you drop off at their Pai office, and their van takes the big bags to Pai. Collect before 12:00, rent for two days, keep a daypack for tonight and tell them you're riding via Chiang Dao.

checkpoints.title: Ride to Chiang Dao
checkpoints.description: ~75 km north on Route 107, ~1.5 h on a wide main road.

checkpoints.title: Chiang Dao Cave
checkpoints.description: Kilometres of caves under the mountain. The lit part is free to wander; a lantern guide takes you into the dark chambers full of stalactites and Buddha shrines.

checkpoints.title: Wat Tham Pha Plong
checkpoints.description: Quiet meditation temple ~510 steps up the mountainside, with a view across to Doi Luang Chiang Dao. Keep your voice down.

checkpoints.title: Chiang Dao hot spring
checkpoints.description: Basic hot pools are free; the Japanese-style garden costs a little more.

checkpoints.title: Sunset at Chiang Dao Mountain View
checkpoints.description: Resort café facing the limestone wall of Doi Luang Chiang Dao (2,225 m), known for sunset dinners. It has rooms, so sleep here (book ahead: Thai long weekend).

days.day: Saturday, 5th December 2026 - Over the mountains to Pai

checkpoints.title: Book the Laos trains!
checkpoints.description: Laos–China Railway tickets go on sale ~7 days ahead and December trains sell out. Today: Luang Prabang → Vang Vieng (12th). Tomorrow: Vang Vieng → Vientiane (13th). LCR Ticket app: sign up with email, add passports, pay by Visa. Plan B: 12Go (needs passport scans).

checkpoints.title: Ride to Pai
checkpoints.description: Back south to Mae Malai, then Route 1095 and its famous 762 curves over the mountains: ~130 km, 3.5–4.5 h with stops. The shorter back road via Muang Khong turns into ~27 km of rough dirt track: not on rental scooters.

checkpoints.title: Pai: bags, check in & laundry
checkpoints.description: Collect the bags at Aya's Pai office and check in (book ahead, it's the long weekend). Drop laundry, same-day at most shops. Keep the scooters until tomorrow morning.

checkpoints.title: Land Split & Pam Bok waterfall
checkpoints.description: A field torn open by an earthquake, where the farmers serve roselle juice and snacks for a donation (until 17:00). Then Pam Bok, a free waterfall at the end of a narrow gorge.

checkpoints.title: Memorial Bridge
checkpoints.description: Old iron bridge over the Pai River from the WWII Japanese supply route, on the road from Chiang Mai. A quick photo stop.

checkpoints.title: Bamboo bridge (Boon Ko Ku So)
checkpoints.description: ~800 m of bamboo walkway across the rice fields to a forest temple.

checkpoints.title: Big Buddha (Wat Phra That Mae Yen)
checkpoints.description: Big white Buddha on the hill east of town, ~350 steps up. The view over the Pai valley makes it a calmer sunset than the canyon.

checkpoints.title: Sunset at Pai Canyon
checkpoints.description: Narrow sandstone ridges with sheer drops on both sides and no railings. Pick a ridge, wait for the sun (~17:45) and bring a torch for the walk out.

checkpoints.title: Walking Street
checkpoints.description: Chaisongkram Road becomes a night market every evening: khao soi, grilled everything, mango sticky rice, then live music in the bars.

checkpoints.title: Sunrise at Yun Lai viewpoint
checkpoints.description: Above the Chinese village of Santichon, often looking down on a sea of mist (sunrise ~06:45).

checkpoints.title: Book the Vang Vieng → Vientiane train
checkpoints.description: Sales for the 13th open today in the LCR Ticket app.

checkpoints.title: Tha Pai hot spring
checkpoints.description: Steaming creek and pools in the forest, opens 08:00.

checkpoints.title: Drop the scooters at Aya
checkpoints.description: Back at the Aya office in Pai, check the scooters over together with the staff and get the deposit back.

checkpoints.title: Van to Chiang Mai
checkpoints.description: Prempracha vans leave Pai bus station hourly for Chiang Mai's Arcade terminal (~3.5 h). Take motion-sickness pills before the 762 curves, not after. Rather skip the morning? A through van to Chiang Rai leaves at 07:00 (~6.5 h, ~€15).

checkpoints.title: Green Bus to Chiang Rai
checkpoints.description: From Arcade Bus Terminal 3 next door: ~13 buses a day until 18:00, 3h20–3h45. Book ahead, it's the Thai long weekend.

checkpoints.title: Check in
checkpoints.description: Sleep near the clock tower: walkable to tonight's night bazaar and tomorrow's Bus Terminal 1.

checkpoints.title: Night Bazaar & clock tower show
checkpoints.description: Food court with a stage: try jim jum, the local clay-pot hot pot. The golden clock tower does a light-and-music show at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00.

days.day: Monday, 7th December 2026 - Chiang Rai temples & Phu Chi Fa

checkpoints.title: White Temple (Wat Rong Khun)
checkpoints.description: Chalermchai Kositpipat's all-white, mirror-studded fantasy temple, 20 min south by Grab. Cross the bridge over the reaching 'hands of hell', find the pop-culture murals inside (no photos) and don't miss the golden toilet building.

checkpoints.title: Blue Temple (Wat Rong Suea Ten)
checkpoints.description: Sapphire-blue hall with a big white Buddha, built by one of Chalermchai's students. Free, 10 min from the centre.

checkpoints.title: Black House (Baan Dam)
checkpoints.description: Thawan Duchanee's dark answer to the White Temple: ~40 black buildings full of horns, skins and bones. 20 min north by Grab, leave the bags at the hotel.

checkpoints.title: Minivan to Phu Chi Fa
checkpoints.description: One van a day, 13:00 from Bus Terminal 1 (platform 1), 3–3.5 h. Or hire a private driver (~€65 per car), who can also take you on to the border tomorrow.

checkpoints.title: Ban Rom Fa Thai
checkpoints.description: Village at the foot of Phu Chi Fa: simple bungalows, or a tent with bedding. Book ahead, the long weekend (7 Dec is the holiday in lieu) fills it and pushes prices up. Ask your host tonight to book a car to Chiang Khong for tomorrow: no bus goes there.

days.day: Tuesday, 8th December 2026 - Phu Chi Fa sunrise & across to Laos

checkpoints.title: Sunrise at Phu Chi Fa
checkpoints.description: Songthaew up to the car park, then ~20 min on a steep path (torch!) to the cliff tip. Sunrise ~06:45 over a sea of mist filling the valleys of Laos; the cliff itself is on the Thai side of the border.

checkpoints.title: Car to Chiang Khong
checkpoints.description: 74 km down to the border, ~1.5 h. No car? The morning van back to Chiang Rai (reportedly 09:00) and the hourly bus to Chiang Khong get you to the border by mid-afternoon.

checkpoints.title: Cross at Friendship Bridge IV
checkpoints.description: Thai exit stamp → mandatory shuttle bus over the Mekong → Lao immigration. The Lao eVisa is accepted here; otherwise visa on arrival with a passport photo and clean USD notes (~€1 extra on weekends). ASEAN passports are visa-free.

checkpoints.title: Huay Xai: check in & get kip
checkpoints.description: Tuk-tuk into town (~15 min) and withdraw kip at a BCEL ATM, Laos runs on cash from here. Ask the guesthouse what time the boat leaves; they also sell tickets incl. the tuk-tuk to the pier for a small commission. Tonight: book a Pakbeng room (December is busy) and stock up on snacks, water and a cushion or sarong for the hard seats.

checkpoints.title: Sunset over the Mekong
checkpoints.description: Riverside dinner looking across at Thailand.

days.day: Wednesday, 9th December 2026 - Slow boat: Huay Xai → Pakbeng

checkpoints.title: Tuk-tuk to the slow boat pier
checkpoints.description: Ticket office is up the steps opposite the boats (passport + cash); stalls sell baguette sandwiches. Board early for seats at the front or middle, the back is next to the loud engine.

checkpoints.title: Slow boat down the Mekong
checkpoints.description: ~7 hours of jungle hills, sandbanks and stilt villages, kids waving from the shore. Barely any signal: cards, books, downloaded playlists, Beerlao from the boat shop. Leaves ~9:00 since Dec 2024 (older guides say 11:00), go by what the pier says.

checkpoints.title: Pakbeng
checkpoints.description: Tiny village where every boat stops for the night. Walk up the hill to the guesthouse, simple dinner on the main street, and order sandwiches for tomorrow.

days.day: Thursday, 10th December 2026 - Slow boat: Pakbeng → Luang Prabang

checkpoints.title: Back to the pier
checkpoints.description: Day-two seats are first come, first served: be there ~45 min before departure.

checkpoints.title: Slow boat to Luang Prabang
checkpoints.description: The longer and prettier day: limestone cliffs, buffalo on the sandbanks and, near the end, the Pak Ou caves packed with thousands of Buddha statues.

checkpoints.title: Arrive in Luang Prabang
checkpoints.description: The boat docks ~10 km upstream of town; shared tuk-tuks wait at the top of the steps (~20 min). Stay on the old-town peninsula.

checkpoints.title: Night market & food alley
checkpoints.description: Handicraft night market on Sisavangvong Road (daily from ~17:00). In the alley next to it: fill-one-plate vegetarian buffets, grilled fish and fruit shakes.

days.day: Friday, 11th December 2026 - Luang Prabang: monks, falls & Phousi

checkpoints.title: Tak Bat (morning alms)
checkpoints.description: Long lines of saffron-robed monks collect sticky rice at dawn. Watch quietly from across the street: no flash, don't block their path. Skip the tourist rice sellers unless you join properly (kneeling, shoulders covered).

checkpoints.title: Morning market & breakfast
checkpoints.description: Small street market by the Royal Palace: river fish, herbs, piles of greens. Then Lao coffee with a baguette or a bowl of khao piak (rice noodle soup).

checkpoints.title: Kuang Si Falls
checkpoints.description: Turquoise limestone pools stepping down through the jungle, ~45 min away by shared van or tuk-tuk. Go early before the tour groups, swim in the lower pools and take the steep side trail to the top of the main fall. Free the Bears sanctuary sits at the entrance.

checkpoints.title: Lao lunch
checkpoints.description: Try larb, mok pa (fish steamed in banana leaf) and jeow bong chili paste with sticky rice.

checkpoints.title: Wat Xieng Thong
checkpoints.description: The most beautiful temple in Laos (1560): roofs sweeping almost to the ground and the glass-mosaic 'tree of life' on the back wall. Then walk to the tip of the peninsula where the Nam Khan meets the Mekong and cross the seasonal bamboo bridge if it's up.

checkpoints.title: Sunset boat on the Mekong
checkpoints.description: One-hour sunset cruise, boats wait along the riverbank. Skip it if two days on the slow boat were enough.

checkpoints.title: Royal Palace Museum (Haw Kham)
checkpoints.description: The last Lao king's palace (1904), with the gilded Haw Pha Bang temple in its grounds, right below Phousi. No shorts or bare shoulders, no photos inside.

checkpoints.title: Sunset on Mount Phousi
checkpoints.description: ~330 steps up to the golden stupa for sunset over the Mekong and the old town. It gets crowded, be at the top by 17:15.

checkpoints.title: Dinner at Manda de Laos
checkpoints.description: Lao dishes around old lotus ponds lit by candles. Book a table.

checkpoints.title: Drinks at Utopia
checkpoints.description: Garden bar on the Nam Khan. The town shuts at ~23:00; the famous after-party is, of all places, the bowling alley.

days.day: Saturday, 12th December 2026 - Train to Vang Vieng

checkpoints.title: Slow morning & check out
checkpoints.description: Last coffee by the Mekong. Leave the bags at reception for one more stroll.

checkpoints.title: To Luang Prabang station
checkpoints.description: ~12 km out of town (~25 min). Be there 45 min early: passport check and airport-style security (knives, lighters and sprays can get confiscated).

checkpoints.title: Train to Vang Vieng
checkpoints.description: C91, ~1 h 10 min of tunnels and karst peaks. Times from the 2026 timetable, double-check in the app.

checkpoints.title: Blue Lagoon 1 & Tham Phu Kham cave
checkpoints.description: Rent scooters or a buggy and ride ~7 km west across the river. Jump from the tree into the turquoise lagoon, then climb ~15 min to the cave with its reclining Buddha (phone torch needed).

checkpoints.title: Nam Xay viewpoint
checkpoints.description: Steep 30–40 min scramble (proper shoes) to the famous motorbike on the summit, the whole karst valley below. Stay for sunset, bring a torch for the way down.

checkpoints.title: Dinner by the Nam Song
checkpoints.description: Riverside bars and restaurants facing the karst cliffs. Want the sunrise balloon? Book it in town tonight.

checkpoints.title: Sunrise hot air balloon
checkpoints.description: Float over the river and karst peaks at sunrise. Book the evening before, compare operators.

checkpoints.title: Tham Nam water-cave tubing
checkpoints.description: Tuk-tuk ~13 km north and pull yourself on a tube along a rope into the Tham Nam water cave (head torch included). ~2–3 h with the ride, back in time for the train. The full kayak + tubing tours take most of the day.

checkpoints.title: To Vang Vieng station
checkpoints.description: Short tuk-tuk ride from town; be there 45 min early for security.

checkpoints.title: Train to Vientiane
checkpoints.description: C91, ~55 min. Vientiane station is ~14 km out: taxi (LOCA app) or the station bus into town (~30 min).

checkpoints.title: COPE Visitor Centre
checkpoints.description: Free and powerful: Laos is the most bombed country per capita in history, and COPE makes prosthetics for people still hurt by the leftover bombs.

checkpoints.title: Patuxai
checkpoints.description: Vientiane's 'Arc de Triomphe', built in the 60s with US cement meant for an airport runway. Climb up for the view down Lane Xang Avenue.

checkpoints.title: Pha That Luang
checkpoints.description: The golden stupa and national symbol of Laos. Next door, Wat That Luang Tai has a giant golden reclining Buddha.

checkpoints.title: Wat Si Saket
checkpoints.description: Vientiane's oldest surviving temple (1818); its cloister walls hold thousands of tiny Buddha statues.

checkpoints.title: Mekong riverside & night market
checkpoints.description: Sunset on the river promenade by Chao Anouvong Park, where half the city does open-air aerobics. Then the night market stalls along the river.

checkpoints.title: Farewell dinner & part ways
checkpoints.description: Last big Lao dinner together, e.g. Kualao with traditional music and dance. Flying out? Wattay airport is ~15 min from the centre. Staying a day longer? Pha That Luang, Wat Si Saket and the COPE Visitor Centre.

days.day: Extra day 1 (before or after the trip) - Bangkok: temples, bikes & boats

checkpoints.title: Night train from Vientiane
checkpoints.description: After the trip: train #134 leaves Vientiane's Khamsavath station (not the Lao–China railway one, ~10 km apart) at 18:25 and gets into Krung Thep Aphiwat at 07:20. There's only one sleeper car, so book early on 12Go or the SRT D-Ticket site, or fly from Wattay (~1h15). Fill in a new TDAC arrival card first. Doing Bangkok before the trip? Fly in and do these two days before Chiang Mai.

checkpoints.title: Grand Palace & the Emerald Buddha
checkpoints.description: Thailand's royal compound: gilded spires, guardian giants and the small jade Emerald Buddha in Wat Phra Kaew. Go at opening, before the heat and the tour buses. Anyone outside saying it's closed today is running a scam.

checkpoints.title: Wat Pho
checkpoints.description: Next door: the 46 m golden reclining Buddha with mother-of-pearl soles. This is where Thai massage was codified, and the temple school still gives massages in the grounds. Lunch afterwards at the Tha Tien market by the pier.

checkpoints.title: Co van Kessel bike tour
checkpoints.description: Bike tours through the alleys, markets and canal-side neighbourhoods most visitors never find. They start from the old pier building at Tha Phra Chan, ~15 min walk north. CO Original: 3 h, 08:00 or 13:00; the Extended tour adds a longtail boat (4.5 h). Book on their site, free cancellation until 24 h before.

checkpoints.title: Ferry to Wat Arun
checkpoints.description: Walk ~20 min south (or Grab) back to Tha Tien pier; the cross-river ferry goes every few minutes.

checkpoints.title: Wat Arun
checkpoints.description: The Temple of Dawn: a towering prang covered in Chinese porcelain flowers, with steep steps up to a river view. Last entry 17:30, then stay by the river for sunset (~17:50).

checkpoints.title: Boat to ICONSIAM
checkpoints.description: The river is Bangkok's best public transport. The blue-flag tourist boat leaves Wat Arun pier every 30 min until ~19:40; the Chao Phraya Express runs up and down the river all day (~€0.50 a ride; orange flag only at weekday rush hours, yellow flag in the daytime).

checkpoints.title: ICONSIAM
checkpoints.description: Riverside mega-mall. SookSiam on the ground floor is an indoor floating market with food and crafts from all 77 provinces, the River Park terrace looks back at the skyline, and the water show runs at 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00.

checkpoints.title: Chinatown street food
checkpoints.description: Yaowarat Road after dark: neon signs, smoking woks and plastic stools, ~15 min by Grab from ICONSIAM (or MRT to Wat Mangkon). Nai Ek's peppery rolled noodles, grilled seafood at T&K, crispy oyster omelette at Nai Mong Hoi Thod (closed Mon–Tue). Many stalls take Mondays off.

checkpoints.title: Train to Ayutthaya
checkpoints.description: Rapid trains from Krung Thep Aphiwat take ~1 h: #135 07:10, #111 07:30 or #75 08:45. 3rd class is unreserved, buy at the station on the day (online sales close the day before).

checkpoints.title: Ferry & bikes into the old city
checkpoints.description: Walk to the river opposite the station, take the little ferry across to the island and rent bicycles there. The ruins are spread out but the island is flat; tuk-tuks can be hired by the hour.

checkpoints.title: Wat Mahathat
checkpoints.description: The Buddha head grown into the roots of a tree, among rows of headless Buddhas left from the Burmese sack of 1767. Crouch for photos: your head shouldn't be higher than the Buddha's.

checkpoints.title: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
checkpoints.description: Three bell-shaped chedis in a row: the royal temple of the old capital and Ayutthaya's postcard view.

checkpoints.title: Wat Lokayasutharam
checkpoints.description: A 42 m reclining Buddha out in the open, usually wrapped in a saffron sash. Free, on the island's west side.

checkpoints.title: Boat noodles & roti sai mai
checkpoints.description: Ayutthaya's specialities: small bowls of rich boat noodles, then roti sai mai (candy-floss threads rolled in thin pancakes) for dessert. Slow afternoon in the shade.

checkpoints.title: Sunset at Wat Chaiwatthanaram
checkpoints.description: Khmer-style towers on the riverbank west of the island, the most beautiful ruin at sunset (~17:50). Open until 18:30.

checkpoints.title: Train back to Bangkok
checkpoints.description: #102 19:16 or #22 21:21 to Krung Thep Aphiwat (~1 h). Doing Bangkok before the trip? Skip the return: sleepers #9 (19:45) and #13 (21:07) to Chiang Mai stop here and arrive at 07:15 / 08:45. Book the berths ahead.
